sentences.ar: إحنا هندخل على طول في الموضوع وناخد رحلة ممتعة جدا
sentences.en: We'll dive straight into the topic and take a very enjoyable journey.

sentences.ar: هنبدأ فيها من الأساسيات البسيطة لـpandas DataFrames لحد ما نوصل لإزاي نبني Database Pipelines قوية ومتينة نقدر نعتمد عليها
sentences.en: We'll start from the simple basics of pandas DataFrames and go all the way to building strong, solid database pipelines we can rely on.

sentences.ar: الشرح ده متصمم عشان ينقلنا من أي فوضى في الديتا للتحكم الكامل فيها خطوة بخطوة
sentences.en: This explainer is designed to move us from any data chaos to full control over it, step by step.

sentences.ar: وعشان نكون منظمين دي خريطة الطريق بتاعتنا
sentences.en: To stay organized, here is our roadmap.

sentences.ar: هنبدأ بأساسيات الـDataFrame والفلترة وبعدين هندخل على الـgrouping ومشاكل الـmerge
sentences.en: We'll start with DataFrame basics and filtering, then move to grouping and merge problems.

sentences.ar: بعدها هنكشف أسرار تظبيط الأداء وطرق التوصيل بالـdatabase وهندخل في سباق سرعة الـbulk load
sentences.en: Then we'll reveal the secrets of performance tuning and ways to connect to the database, and enter the bulk-load speed race.

sentences.ar: وفي الآخر هنختم بإزاي نأمن الاتصالات بتاعتنا ونعمل الاختبارات
sentences.en: Finally we'll wrap up with how to secure our connections and write tests.

sentences.ar: القسم الأول DataFrame Basics and Filtering
sentences.en: Section one: DataFrame Basics and Filtering.

sentences.ar: خلونا نخط الأساس المتين مع pandas
sentences.en: Let's lay a solid foundation with pandas.

sentences.ar: خلونا نتخيل الـDataFrame كجدول حي قدامنا
sentences.en: Let's picture the DataFrame as a living table in front of us.

sentences.ar: هو في الأساس جدول ثنائي الأبعاد ليه index على الشمال بيحددوا الصفوف وcolumns أو أعمدة فوق
sentences.en: It is basically a two-dimensional table, with an index on the left that identifies the rows and columns on top.

sentences.ar: ومن تحت خالص اللي شايل الأرقام دي كلها وبيخليها تشتغل هو NumPy array
sentences.en: And deep underneath, what holds all these numbers and makes them work is a NumPy array.

sentences.ar: أول ما نمسك أي داتا جديدة أوامر بسيطة زي info وdescribe هي أدوات الاستكشاف الأولى بتاعتنا عشان نفهم الأنواع ونشوف لو في أي قيم ناقصة
sentences.en: As soon as we get any new data, simple commands like info and describe are our first exploration tools, to understand the types and see if any values are missing.

sentences.ar: ولما نيجي نفلتر الداتا لو حابين نختار بالمكان بنستخدم iloc لكن لو بالاسم بنستخدم loc
sentences.en: When we filter data, to select by position we use iloc, but by name we use loc.

sentences.ar: وزي ما احنا شايفين قدامنا الصفوف اللي مش بتحقق الشرط بتختفي على طول
sentences.en: As we can see, the rows that don't meet the condition disappear right away.

sentences.ar: النقطة المحورية والسر هنا هو
sentences.en: The key point and the secret here is:

sentences.ar: يعني لو عندنا شروط مركبة استخدام np.select أسرع وأنظف بكتير جدا من إننا نستخدم apply ونمشي على الداتا صف في صف
sentences.en: With compound conditions, using np.select is much faster and cleaner than using apply and walking over the data row by row.

sentences.ar: لإن ده بيبطأ الأداء جدا
sentences.en: Because that slows performance down a lot.

sentences.ar: القسم الثاني Grouping, Merged Traps and Cleaning
sentences.en: Section two: Grouping, Merge Traps and Cleaning.

sentences.ar: يلا نبدأ نجمع الداتا ونربطها ببعضها
sentences.en: Let's start aggregating the data and joining it together.

sentences.ar: بس خلو بالكو إحنا داخلين على منطقة فيها فخاخ خطيرة جدا
sentences.en: But watch out: we're entering an area full of very dangerous traps.

sentences.ar: الـgroupby فكرته ببساطة بتتلخص في 3 خطوات split، apply، combine
sentences.en: The idea of groupby boils down to three steps: split, apply, combine.

sentences.ar: خلونا نتخيل الصفوف وهي بتتحرك وتتوزع في buckets أو groups المختلفة حسب الفئة دي مرحلة الـsplit
sentences.en: Picture the rows moving and being distributed into different buckets or groups by category; that's the split stage.

sentences.ar: بعدين بنحسب المجموع أو المتوسط لكل bucket ودي مرحلة الـapply
sentences.en: Then we compute the sum or the mean for each bucket; that's the apply stage.

sentences.ar: وفي الآخر بنجمعهم في خطوة الـcombine
sentences.en: Finally we gather them in the combine step.

sentences.ar: الفرق الجوهري هنا أن agg بترجع صف واحد لكل مجموعة لكن transform بتحتفظ بنفس شكل وحجم الجدول الأصلي
sentences.en: The key difference: agg returns one row per group, while transform keeps the same shape and size as the original table.

sentences.ar: وده بيودينا لعطل ممكن يدمر الشغل
sentences.en: And that leads us to a bug that can wreck the work.

sentences.ar: لو بصينا على عدد الصفوف كان 6 صفوف قبل الـmerge فجأة ضرب وبقى رقم ضخم جدا بالأحمر بعده
sentences.en: Looking at the row count: it was 6 rows before the merge, and suddenly it blew up into a huge red number after it.

sentences.ar: ده اسمه الـfan-out error
sentences.en: This is called the fan-out error.

sentences.ar: وبيحصل لما المفاتيح او الـkeys تتكرر وتضاعف الصفوف بشكل احنا مش متوقعينه
sentences.en: It happens when the keys repeat and multiply the rows in a way we don't expect.

sentences.ar: وعشان نتفادى الكارثة دي دايما بنستخدم validate بتساوي many_to_one عشان يرمي error بدري لو في مشكلة
sentences.en: To avoid this disaster we always use validate equals many_to_one, so it throws an error early if there's a problem.

sentences.ar: وindicator بتساوي True عشان نعرف كل صف جاي منين بالظبط
sentences.en: And indicator equals True, so we know exactly where each row came from.

sentences.ar: تنظيف الداتا مش معناه أننا نمسح وخلاص
sentences.en: Cleaning data doesn't mean we just delete and that's it.

sentences.ar: أكبر غلطة هي استخدام dropna على عماها لأننا ممكن نخسر 50% من الداتا بتاعتنا في ثانية
sentences.en: The biggest mistake is using dropna blindly, because we could lose 50% of our data in a second.

sentences.ar: التنظيف ده عبارة عن قرارات مدروسة زي أننا نحول النصوص الفاضية لـNaN أو نمسح العمود بس لو ناقص فيه أكتر من 50% داتا
sentences.en: Cleaning is a set of deliberate decisions, like converting empty strings to NaN, or dropping a column only if more than 50% of its data is missing.

sentences.ar: ونعلم على الـoutliers لو الـz-score بتاعهم معدي 3
sentences.en: And we flag outliers if their z-score exceeds 3.

sentences.ar: ولما نيجي نبني profile كامل للعميل زي Customer 360 بنستخدم pd.concat خطوة بخطوة ونرأي بعدد الصفوف دايما
sentences.en: When we build a full customer profile like Customer 360, we use pd.concat step by step and always watch the row count.

sentences.ar: القسم الثالث Secrets of Performance Tuning
sentences.en: Section three: Secrets of Performance Tuning.

sentences.ar: هنغير التركيز بتاعنا دلوقتي للسرعة واستهلاك الميموري
sentences.en: Now we shift our focus to speed and memory consumption.

sentences.ar: في سباق بين طرق مختلفة لكتابة الكود
sentences.en: There's a race between different ways of writing the code.

sentences.ar: القاعدة الذهبية في pandas هي دايما نستخدم الـvectorization
sentences.en: The golden rule in pandas is: always use vectorization.

sentences.ar: زي ما احنا شايفين في السباق ده الـPython loop بطيء جدا
sentences.en: As we see in this race, the Python loop is very slow.

sentences.ar: الـlambda apply أسرع شوية لكن np.where اللي شغال vectorization بيكسب باكتساح وبياخد المركز الأول
sentences.en: The lambda apply is a bit faster, but np.where, running vectorized, wins by a landslide and takes first place.

sentences.ar: السر كمان مش بس في كود ده في الداتا نفسه
sentences.en: The secret isn't only in the code; it's in the data itself.

sentences.ar: لو غيرنا نوع العمود بين int64 اللي بياخد 8 bytes لـint16 اللي بياخد 2 bytes أو حولنا النصوص المتكررة لـcategory هنوفر كمية ميموري خرافية
sentences.en: If we change a column's type from int64, which takes 8 bytes, to int16, which takes 2 bytes, or convert repeated strings to category, we save a huge amount of memory.

sentences.ar: القسم الرابع Database Connection Methods
sentences.en: Section four: Database Connection Methods.

sentences.ar: ودلوقتي هنطلع من عالم pandas وندخل في عالم الـdatabase
sentences.en: Now we leave the world of pandas and enter the world of the database.

sentences.ar: عندنا 4 طرق أساسية نقدر نكلم بيهم الـdatabase من جوا Python
sentences.en: We have four main ways to talk to the database from inside Python.

sentences.ar: جدول المقارنة ده مهم جدا وما ينفعش نتجاهله بأي شكل
sentences.en: This comparison table is very important and we can't ignore it in any way.

sentences.ar: الـraw driver سريع جدا بس شغله يدوي تماما
sentences.en: The raw driver is very fast but its work is fully manual.

sentences.ar: الـSQLAlchemy Core ممتاز ومناسب جدا للـpipelines
sentences.en: SQLAlchemy Core is excellent and very well suited for pipelines.

sentences.ar: الـORM عظيم في تطبيقات الويب بس لازم ناخد بالنا من فخ الـN+1 queries اللي بيعمل loop استعلامات قاتل
sentences.en: The ORM is great for web apps, but we must watch out for the N+1 queries trap, which runs a deadly loop of queries.

sentences.ar: وأخيرا pandas.read_sql وده أحسن حاجة للتحليل
sentences.en: And finally pandas.read_sql, the best option for analysis.

sentences.ar: النقطة المحورية هنا أكبر غلطة هي أننا ندخل parameters بإيدينا جوه الـSQL
sentences.en: The key point here: the biggest mistake is typing parameters by hand inside the SQL.

sentences.ar: لازم نستخدم الطرق الآمنة عشان نمنع الـSQL injection تماما
sentences.en: We must use the safe methods to fully prevent SQL injection.

sentences.ar: القسم الخامس The bulk load speed race
sentences.en: Section five: The bulk load speed race.

sentences.ar: جاهزين للإثارة؟ إحنا دلوقتي في قسم التحميل الجماعي
sentences.en: Ready for some excitement? We're now in the bulk-loading section.

sentences.ar: وده حرفياً سباق ضد الزمن عشان ننقل 10,000 صف بأسرع شكل ممكن
sentences.en: This is literally a race against time to move 10,000 rows as fast as possible.

sentences.ar: الأرقام بالضبط هنا هتصدمكم
sentences.en: The exact numbers here will shock you.

sentences.ar: السر كله في تقليل الرحلات للـdatabase
sentences.en: The whole secret is reducing round-trips to the database.

sentences.ar: لو عملنا 10,000 حركة insert فردية هتاخد حوالي 60 ثانية من الانتظار الممل
sentences.en: If we do 10,000 individual inserts, it takes about 60 seconds of boring waiting.

sentences.ar: بـpandas.to_sql بتنزل لـ3 ثواني
sentences.en: With pandas.to_sql it drops to 3 seconds.

sentences.ar: لو استخدمنا executemany هتنزل لثانيتين
sentences.en: If we use executemany it drops to 2 seconds.

sentences.ar: ولو استخدمنا multi-row VALUES هتبقى نص ثانية بس
sentences.en: And with multi-row VALUES it's just half a second.

sentences.ar: والـLOAD DATA INFILE بياخد واحد من عشرة ثانية كأنه flash
sentences.en: And LOAD DATA INFILE takes a tenth of a second, like a flash.

sentences.ar: وعشان التحميل يبقى آمن ويتعاد من غير مشاكل بنستخدم تقنية الـupsert يعني حدث الداتا لو موجودة وضفها لو مش موجودة
sentences.en: To make loading safe and re-runnable without problems, we use upsert: update the data if it exists and add it if it doesn't.

sentences.ar: وده بيودينا لدورة الـETL كاملة
sentences.en: That brings us to the full ETL cycle.

sentences.ar: أول خطوة extract بنقرأ الداتا على دفعات باستخدام chunksize
sentences.en: Step one, extract: we read the data in batches using chunksize.

sentences.ar: تاني خطوة transform بننظف الداتا ونحسب اللي احنا عايزين
sentences.en: Step two, transform: we clean the data and compute what we need.

sentences.ar: تالت خطوة load بنستخدم الـupsert في دفعات
sentences.en: Step three, load: we use upsert in batches.

sentences.ar: ورابع حاجة والأهم Update Watermark
sentences.en: And fourth, the most important: update the watermark.

sentences.ar: الـwatermark ده ببساطة هو ذاكرة الـpipeline بيعرفنا آخر داتا تسحبت إمتى عشان المرة الجاية نجيب الجديد بس
sentences.en: The watermark is simply the pipeline's memory: it tells us when data was last pulled, so next time we fetch only what's new.

sentences.ar: ودايماً بنحدثه بعد ما التحميل ينجح بالكامل مش قبله أبداً
sentences.en: And we always update it after the load fully succeeds, never before.

sentences.ar: القسم السادس والأخير Connection Safety, Transactions and Tests
sentences.en: Section six and last: Connection Safety, Transactions and Tests.

sentences.ar: وصلنا لآخر قسم وهنا هنركز على إزاي نحمي الـdatabase من إنها توقع تحت الضغط وإزاي نختبر شغالينا بأمان تام
sentences.en: We've reached the last section; here we focus on protecting the database from collapsing under pressure and testing our work safely.

sentences.ar: فتح اتصال بالـdatabase مكلف وبياخد من 10 ل 50 ميلي ثانية عقاب في كل مرة
sentences.en: Opening a database connection is expensive, costing 10 to 50 milliseconds as a penalty every time.

sentences.ar: الحل السحري هو الـconnection pool ودي ببساطة اتصالات دافية وجاهزة بتتسلف وترجع تاني للـpool
sentences.en: The magic fix is the connection pool: warm, ready connections that are borrowed and returned to the pool.

sentences.ar: الحسبة هنا مهمة جدا عشان ما نعديش الحدود
sentences.en: The math here is very important so we don't exceed the limits.

sentences.ar: لو عندنا 4 سيرفرات ومجموع الاتصالات الأساسية والاحتياطية في كل سيرفر 30 يبقى 4 في 30 بـ120
sentences.en: If we have 4 servers and the base plus backup connections per server total 30, that's 4 times 30, 120.

sentences.ar: الرقم ده آمن جدا لأننا جوه الحد الأقصى الافتراضي لـMySQL اللي هو 151 اتصال
sentences.en: That number is very safe because we're within MySQL's default maximum of 151 connections.

sentences.ar: الـtimeline ده بيشرح transactions بامتياز
sentences.en: This timeline explains transactions perfectly.

sentences.ar: خلونا نتخيل اننا سجلنا الطلب وسجلنا المنتجات وجينا نحدث المخزون فحصلت مشكلة
sentences.en: Imagine we recorded the order and recorded the items, then went to update the stock and a problem occurred.

sentences.ar: هنا بيجي دور الـsavepoint بيخلينا نعمل rollback أو تراجع عن الخطوة الفاشلة دي بس
sentences.en: This is where the savepoint comes in: it lets us roll back just that failed step.

sentences.ar: ونكمل بقية الدفعة ونعملها commit بأمان من غير ما نخسر الشغل كله
sentences.en: And continue the rest of the batch and commit it safely, without losing all the work.

sentences.ar: وعشان ننام واحنا متطمنين لازم نختبر الكود
sentences.en: And to sleep soundly, we must test the code.

sentences.ar: هرم الاختبارات بيبدأ بـunit tests سريعة باستخدام Mock وبعدين integration tests على database حقيقية
sentences.en: The testing pyramid starts with fast unit tests using Mock, then integration tests on a real database.

sentences.ar: التريكة العبقرية هنا إننا بنحط كل اختبار جوة transaction بيتعمل لها rollback في الآخر
sentences.en: The clever trick here is putting each test inside a transaction that gets rolled back at the end.

sentences.ar: ده بيضمن إن كل اختبار يبدأ والـdatabase نظيفة تماما وما فيهاش أي ديتا من الاختبار اللي قبله
sentences.en: That guarantees every test starts with a perfectly clean database, with no data from the previous test.

sentences.ar: وطبعا بنعمل assertions واضحة يعني لو السعر 999 والكمية 2 الناتج لازم يكون 1998 بالظبط
sentences.en: And of course we write clear assertions: if the price is 999 and the quantity 2, the result must be exactly 1998.

sentences.ar: الشرح ده غطى رحلة الداتا من أول ما كانت فوضى في pandas لحد ما دخلت الـdatabase بأمان وسرعة
sentences.en: This explainer covered the data's journey from chaos in pandas until it entered the database safely and quickly.

sentences.ar: إيه اللي ممكن يحصل للـdata pipeline بتاعنا لو فجأة الطلبات زادت بشكل رهيب وتخطت السعة القصوى للـpool اللي احنا لسه حاسبينه
sentences.en: What could happen to our data pipeline if orders suddenly surged and exceeded the maximum pool capacity we just calculated?

sentences.ar: ده اللي هنكتشفه في الشرح اللي جاي شكرا جدا ليكم
sentences.en: That's what we'll discover in the next explainer. Thank you very much.

glossary.rule: Explain the term in Egyptian Arabic the first time it appears; then use the original term naturally, in Latin script, inside Arabic sentences.
glossary.register_ar: Natural Egyptian, clear, calm, professional. Use إحنا and خلّينا نشوف and ببساطة where they help. No heavy Modern Standard Arabic. No exaggerated slang. Numbers are spoken naturally in Egyptian but displayed as Western digits.
glossary.register_en: Plain, direct, unhurried. Short sentences. No hype, no "imagine that…", no rhetorical questions that are not real prediction prompts. Say the number, then pause for half a beat before the next sentence — the pause is where the viewer reads the screen.
glossary.never_translate_rule: Explain them in Egyptian Arabic the first time they appear, then use the original term naturally.

concepts.def_en: A Python library for tabular data analysis, built around the DataFrame, for loading, cleaning, filtering, grouping and joining data in memory.
concepts.failure: Loading data bigger than RAM into pandas, or looping row by row instead of vectorizing.

concepts.def_en: A pandas table of labeled columns and rows, where each column is a Series of one type.
concepts.failure: Looping over DataFrame rows instead of using vectorized operations.

concepts.def_en: An organized store of data managed by software that lets many users and programs safely read, write and query it.
concepts.failure: Treating a database as a bigger spreadsheet, ignoring keys, constraints and concurrent writes.

concepts.def_en: A chain of automated steps where each stage's output feeds the next, such as extract, transform and load for data.
concepts.failure: Not making steps idempotent, so a rerun duplicates or corrupts data.

concepts.def_en: Combining two sources into one: in pandas/SQL, joining tables on a key; in git, integrating one branch's changes into another.
concepts.failure: Merging on a non-unique key without validate, silently multiplying rows.

concepts.def_en: Keeping only the rows that meet a boolean condition, in pandas with a mask or in SQL with WHERE.
concepts.failure: Filtering after an expensive merge instead of before, or chaining conditions without parentheses.

concepts.def_en: A separate sorted lookup structure on one or more columns that lets a database find rows without scanning the whole table.
concepts.failure: Adding an index on every column; each one slows writes and may never be used.

concepts.def_en: A block of items stored contiguously in memory and accessed by index; dynamic arrays grow by reallocating a larger block.
concepts.failure: Assuming inserting in the middle is cheap, when later elements must all shift.

concepts.def_en: The SQL clause that chooses which columns or expressions to return, and where aliases are created.
concepts.failure: Writing SELECT * in production, pulling columns and resources nobody needs.

concepts.def_en: A join returning more rows than went in, because the join key is not unique on the other side.
concepts.failure: Summing after a join without checking key uniqueness, silently inflating totals.

concepts.def_en: A message or failure signalling that something went wrong; read it first, since it usually names the cause and the location.
concepts.failure: Pasting the error into a search engine without first reading the terminal output.

concepts.def_en: Computing on a whole column or array at once with optimized native code instead of looping row by row.
concepts.failure: Using apply with a lambda row by row, much slower than a vectorized operation.

concepts.def_en: A readable, general-purpose programming language widely used for data analysis, automation, pipelines and AI work.
concepts.failure: Using plain loops over huge data instead of vectorized pandas or SQL operations.

concepts.def_en: A construct that repeats a block of code for each item or until a condition changes.
concepts.failure: Off-by-one bounds, or a condition that never changes, looping forever.

concepts.def_en: Structured Query Language: the standard declarative language for querying and changing data in relational databases by describing what you want.
concepts.failure: Thinking SQL runs in written order; the engine plans execution in its own order.

concepts.def_en: An attack where untrusted input is executed as code or commands, such as SQL injection; parameterized queries keep data separate from code.
concepts.failure: Building queries by concatenating user input into SQL strings instead of parameterizing.

concepts.def_en: Update the row if it exists, insert it if it does not, making loads safe to re-run.
concepts.failure: Upserting without a unique key, so duplicates appear instead of updates.

concepts.def_en: Extract, Transform, Load: pull data from sources, clean and reshape it first, then load the finished result into the target.
concepts.failure: Discarding the raw data after transforming, so mistakes cannot be replayed.

concepts.def_en: A marker of progress: in streams, how long to wait for late events before closing a window; in incremental loads, the last value loaded.
concepts.failure: Setting the watermark too tight drops late events; too loose delays results and bloats state.

concepts.def_en: A widely used open-source relational database that stores data in tables and is queried with SQL.
concepts.failure: Assuming MySQL and PostgreSQL behave identically in SQL dialect and defaults.

concepts.def_en: A named point inside a transaction you can roll back to, undoing only later steps without cancelling the whole transaction.
concepts.failure: Assuming a savepoint commits earlier work; nothing is permanent until the transaction commits.

concepts.def_en: Reverting to a previous known-good state: undoing a failed transaction's changes, or redeploying the last good version.
concepts.failure: Assuming a code rollback also undoes database changes already committed.

concepts.def_en: In git, a saved snapshot of changes with a message; in databases, the step that makes a transaction permanent.
concepts.failure: Committing unrelated changes together with vague messages, making review and rollback hard.

concepts.def_en: A group of database operations treated as one unit: either all succeed together or none take effect.
concepts.failure: Leaving a transaction open too long, holding locks and blocking other sessions.
